STATUS CHECK + STOP.

RAM has fallen to 0.45 GB free of 15.71 GB — the hard-stop zone. Stop all execution now. Do not run anything further; do not start new probes.

I have already verified your landed work on disk myself and it is CORRECT:
- sqlite.py:202-242 `_ensure_ready()` opens on demand and re-runs the FULL open path in __init__'s order: row_factory (226-227), _SCHEMA (232), _migrate (233), commit (234). That is the part a naive fix would have missed. Verified.
- The except branch (235-241) nulls self._conn and closes, so a half-configured connection is never adopted. Verified.
- All 9 read/write call sites route through _ensure_ready() (lines 304, 345, 375, 389, 399, 427, 444, 452, and 200 in __init__). No bare self._conn use survives outside _ensure_ready/_migrate. Verified.
- close() at 457-474 swaps `conn, self._conn = self._conn, None` under the lock and closes outside it, so it is idempotent and safe on a never-opened store. Verified.

So do NOT re-verify or re-edit any of that. Just send your final report now, answering these points in plain text:

1. Your minimal reproduction output — the ACTUAL exception type and message from the pre-fix sqlite post-close read, and the memory result for comparison.
2. Your reachability verdict: LIVE or LATENT, and the file+line evidence that decided it. This is the part I most need and must not accept on plausibility.
3. Whether tests/test_store_close_contract_agent.py was RUN or UNRUN, and if RUN, the exact counts.
4. One thing I want to understand: your docstring at _migrate (244-259) describes a duplicate-column migration race between two processes. Is that a defect you FIXED, only DOCUMENTED, or something you newly DISCOVERED this round? If you only documented it, I want that recorded as a separate open item, not folded into the close() fix.

Then confirm you have left no scratch file behind, anywhere. Do not delete the repo-root _probe_*.py files — those are handled centrally.

You've completed your task and delivered a code fix for sqlite.py verified on disk by myself (the orchestrator), including an execution probe proving end-to-end correctness. The XPASS issue you flagged in test_store_divergence_agent.py has been recorded as follow-up. The team's mission is complete for this round; please confirm with a shutdown_response message before I call team_delete.
